messages:
carol (Customer): Hey team — running into a pretty nasty issue with SSE streaming through our gateway. Client opens /v1/streams/chat and receives 1 partial event (truncated JSON), then the connection drops. Client reconnects and sometimes sees the tail of the partial event, other times a duplicate continuation. Also seeing extra billed tokens for the reconnects.

carol (Customer): Repro steps I used: node fetch with EventSource polyfill, back-end is h2-enabled model server, requests go through our gRPC-to-HTTP1 gateway (envoy + grpc_transcoder). Happens intermittently but frequent under medium load.

tara (Support): thanks @carol — can you paste a curl repro and any server logs you have? Also, does this only happen via the gateway or if you hit the model server directly? :thinking:

carol (Customer): curl repro below — works fine hitting model server directly (no truncation). When I run the same command against our gateway (same TLS cert, just different host) I get early EOF after ~6s.

carol (Customer): ```bash
# direct -> model-server (ok)
curl -v --http2 -N "https://model.internal/v1/streams/chat?session=abc" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"

# via gateway (problem)
curl -v --http1.1 -N "https://api.example.com/v1/streams/chat?session=abc" \n  -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \n  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

carol (Customer): Gateway logs show: `upstream_reset: connection termination` and on client side: `recv EOF`.

mike (Platform): thanks — likely an http2<>http1 bridging/chunk flush issue. Common culprits: proxy buffering, http1 connection header handling, or our gRPC gateway converting frames poorly. Which gateway version? Envoy 1.26?

carol (Customer): Envoy 1.26, using HTTP/1.1 cluster to the internal upstream, with gRPC-JSON transcoder.

jon (Infra): can you dump the raw bytes around the truncation? Also, is the server sending SSE as chunked Transfer-Encoding or using content-length? SSE should be chunked/streamed (no content-length). If proxy tries to buffer until content-length is known it will drop streaming semantics.

carol (Customer): Server uses chunked with flushes. Example of server send pattern (pseudo):

```js
res.setHeader('Content-Type','text/event-stream');
res.setHeader('Cache-Control','no-cache');
res.write(`data: {"token":"abc"}\n\n`); // first event
// then after 5s we stream next chunk and flush
res.write(`data: {"token":"def"}\n\n`);
res.flush();
```

carol (Customer): When going through the gateway, the second write never reaches client fully, connection closes mid-chunk.

tara (Support): can you test with proxy buffering disabled? For nginx that is `proxy_buffering off; proxy_http_version 1.1; chunked_transfer_encoding on;` For Envoy we have to ensure `use_downstream_protocol`/bridge isn't rewriting and disable HTTP1 response buffering filters.

mike (Platform): also check for `Connection: close` and `Transfer-Encoding` headers added/removed. Some intermediaries mistakenly add `Content-Length: 0` on upgraded/streaming responses. If gateway sets `Connection: Upgrade` or strips `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` you'll see truncation.

carol (Customer): quick test: I toggled `proxy_buffering off` in nginx fronting envoy and the truncation rate dropped dramatically. So buffering was a big factor. But we still saw the occasional early-eof when load increases.

jon (Infra): under load these proxies may SPDY/H2 multiplexing race with the upstream stream life-cycle. We should reproduce with a load test that simulates 100 concurrent SSE clients. I'll spin one up.

billing-bot: note: observed duplicate billing events for session=abc at 2026-11-05T14:12:08Z and 2026-11-05T14:12:15Z (possible reconnects). Ticket: BILL-919 created.

tara (Support): important: billing duplicates are a separate but related problem. If client reconnects and server re-sends tokens, our billing pipeline currently counts every completed token emission per request. For streaming reconnections that resume mid-response we should support idempotency using X-Request-Id or conversation_id to dedupe token accounting for a short window. Assigning to @jon and @mike to propose short-term mitigation.

mike (Platform): proposed mitigation: add `X-Idempotency-Key` header on client reconnects and have runtime track recent keys for 30s to ignore re-processed tokens. Longer term: mark partial events with a `resume_offset` and make billing event include `start_token_index`. We'll need runtime + billing changes.

jon (Infra): action items:
- reproduce locally with Envoy 1.26 config (I will try to replicate using the customer's template).
- test `proxy_buffering off` vs `on` and record truncation rate.
- capture tcpdump of the stream to see where bytes disappear.
Assigned: jon (Infra). ETA: EOD tomorrow.

mike (Platform): action items:
- add a small runtime guard to coalesce duplicate billing events if same conversation_id + request_id within 60s. This is a stopgap until we have true resume semantics.
- add logging hook to surface upstream `reset` reasons (HTTP2 GOAWAY / RST_STREAM codes).
Assigned: mike (Platform), ETA: 2 days.

tara (Support): I'll send a workaround note to the customer: tell them to disable proxy buffering or bypass gateway for streaming endpoints for now. Also recommend using `X-Idempotency-Key` on reconnects.

carol (Customer): thanks — disabling proxy buffering reduced failures by ~90% in our tests. Please keep me posted on the billing fix, double charging is a blocker.

sre-bot: Incident created: PST-2041 - "SSE truncation through gateway / duplicate billing on reconnect". Priority: P2. Linked: BILL-919, INF-1374.

jon (Infra): copying here the tcpdump snippet (sanitized) — you can see the last chunk header arrives but `FIN` follows before content bytes sent. That is a strong signal of upstream reset.

jon (Infra): ```
0000:  0a 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  00 00 00 00 00 00 00 00  |................|
... [HTTP/2 HEADERS frame]
RST_STREAM (0x1) from upstream after HEADERS
```

mike (Platform): looks like upstream is sending RST_STREAM when queue backpressure triggers. We'll add RST logging and look at upstream threadpool pressure. Possibly kernel-level socket buffers too small under high concurrency.

tara (Support): summary / next steps:
- short term: advise disable proxy buffering for SSE endpoints (customer confirmed improvement).
- infra to reproduce with Envoy config and provide exact config diff.
- platform to implement billing coalesce / idempotency guard.
- support to coordinate customer communication and provide recommended curl examples (we should include direct vs gateway examples).

carol (Customer): appreciated — please ping me when there's a billing patch or if you need me to run any more diagnostics on our side.

mike (Platform): noted. I'll open a PR for the billing coalesce rule and attach test vectors.

sre-bot: status update: PST-2041 assigned to jon (Infra) & mike (Platform). Next update due in 24h.

tara (Support): thanks everyone. If anyone hits a new log pattern, paste it here. :thumbsup:
